reasons.A: Periodic, semicolon-joined sentences and earnest Edwardian register come close, but clauses are shorter and more evenly balanced than the passage's long accumulating, self-qualifying sentences.
reasons.B: Mostly short, plain modern sentences with a personal-memoir stance; it lacks the passage's long stacked subordinate clauses, semicolons and period diction.
reasons.C: Longest, most heavily qualified sentences with inserted hedges ('so to speak', 'I think', 'one feels') and semicolon chains closest to the passage's movement and period feel, though the closing similes are a little more ornamental than the author's.
